North Island · BC provincial · 2017 → 2024, voting area by voting area

The riding that really did move

Its federal twin barely shifted and flipped on a split. This one shifted for real: a seat New Democrats had held since 2005 broke to Conservative Anna Kindy by 639 votes — while the NDP's own vote went up. Scroll — we'll walk the map.

⏱43rd BC General Election · October 19, 2024 · official results
Scroll
2024 result · by voting area

1 · Where you are

Two decades orange, then this

North Island runs from Campbell River to Cape Scott — mill towns, fishing harbours, the Broughton islands, and the homelands of the Kwakwaka'wakw nations. The NDP held it for nineteen years: Claire Trevena from 2005, Michele Babchuk from 2020.

Every shape is a voting area, coloured by its polling place's 2024 election-day count. Blue is Conservative Anna Kindy. Orange is Babchuk. In 2024, for the first time since 2005, blue won: 47.1 to 44.9.

Election-day ballots shown on the map; advance and mail ballots are counted riding-wide and included in every riding total we quote.

2 · What changed

This time the tide was real

Same map, recoloured by how much the combined right vote — BC Liberal plus Conservative in 2020, Conservative alone in 2024 — grew in each place. Federally, Gunn's share barely moved. Provincially, the right rose in every town and village on this map — roughly nine to fourteen points in the towns.

47.1Kindy 2024 — vs 30.0 for the combined right in 2020
639votes — the margin that ended 19 years

The BC United collapse delivered the old Liberal vote to the Conservatives — and the column kept growing beyond the sum of its parts.

3 · Campbell River

Half the riding lives here

The aquaculture capital of Canada, a union mill town in living memory, and Babchuk's home council seat. Election day here broke 49.6 to 43.2 for Kindy — a twelve-point rightward move from 2020 in the city that casts more election-day ballots than everywhere else combined.

12point rise in the right's e-day share since 2020
9,364election-day ballots in Campbell River, 2024

The 2029 federal fish-farm ban hangs over more than a thousand local jobs — the same material anxiety that moved this city federally.

4 · The resource belt

The villages ran at double the tide

Sayward up 29 points. Woss and Tahsis up 24. Gold River up 22. The logging and mill villages didn't drift right — they lurched, exactly like their federal twins. Woss voted 60% NDP in 2017; by 2024 it was 28.

+29Sayward's right-of-centre shift, 2020 → 2024
60→28Woss NDP share, 2017 vs 2024

The coastal harvest is down more than 40% since 2019; an 8-month strike shut North Island logging into 2026. Every curtailment here has names attached.

5 · The Morton wave

2020's green flood, and where it went

Now the map shows the 2020 Green vote — Alexandra Morton's run. The Broughton's most famous campaigner against open-net fish farms took the islands by storm: Alert Bay went 58% Green, Sointula 64, Cortes 67. It looked like NDP collapse. It wasn't — it was borrowed.

In 2024, with Morton gone, most of it came home: Alert Bay 58% NDP, Sointula 59, Cortes 63. But not all the way home — Alert Bay was 77% NDP in 2017.

58Alert Bay Green % in 2020 — Morton's wave
19points of 2017 NDP support not yet recovered there

6 · The islands held

The fortress the tide couldn't take

Quadra Island: 60% NDP on election day. Cortes: 63. Alert Bay, Sointula, the Broughton communities: all still orange, all right-share below 26% even in the Conservatives' best year in a generation. The wall stands — but it votes at small-island numbers.

60.3Quadra Island NDP %, election day 2024
<26right-of-centre share on every island

7 · Port Hardy and the ER

The wound that elected a doctor

Port Hardy's emergency room has been closed overnight since January 2023. Patients drive 45 km to Port McNeill; in March 2024 the Gwa'sala-'Nakwaxda'xw Nations declared a state of emergency after eleven deaths. Anna Kindy is a physician who once practised here. That is the campaign, in one sentence.

And yet: Port Hardy still voted 50% NDP on election day. The north end holds — Port McNeill is where the right now runs 56.

49.6Port Hardy NDP %, e-day 2024
56.4Port McNeill right %, e-day 2024

The $45M Port Hardy Hospital upgrade was announced in March 2026 — with 24/7 emergency service still not restored.

8 · The whole picture

The NDP vote rose. The seat fell.

Babchuk won a thousand more votes in 2024 than in 2020 — 13,461 against 12,467 — and lost, because the Conservative electorate grew by six thousand seven hundred as turnout snapped back and the right consolidated. The Greens fell to 8%. There is no split left to squeeze.

This seat is now a pure two-way fight, and 639 votes is the whole distance.

14,100Kindy 2024
13,461Babchuk 2024 — up ~1,000 on 2020, still short

What actually happened here

Not a protest, not a split — a realignment. The old BC Liberal vote, the PPC-style fringe, and a slice of former New Democrats consolidated into one Conservative column, hardest in the towns that work in the woods and on the water.

realignment, n.

When a coalition changes shape rather than size: North Island's right went from 35% (2017, Liberal) to 30% (2020, split) to 47% (2024, Conservative) — while the NDP never left the 45-to-51 band. The floor held. The ceiling moved.

Held: NDP raw vote — 13,461, up ~1,000 on 2020 The islands — 58–73% NDP Port Hardy — 50% on e-day
Gone: Green vote — 19.3% → 8.0% BC Liberals as a brand The resource villages — Woss 60% NDP → 28%

What to do about it · October 21, 2028

The Beat-Kindy Playbook

The arithmetic, one more time — every play starts from these numbers.

14,100Kindy
13,461NDP
639the gap
2,397the whole Green pool
1

Fight it as the two-way it now is

There is no third-party squeeze left — the Greens hold 8%. Three hundred and twenty switchers, or about 640 net new NDP voters, wins the seat. Every play below is persuasion of the soft middle or turnout of the base. Nothing else moves this riding.

2

Neutralize the doctor on her own ward

Kindy's brand is the ER file, and Port Hardy's overnight closure — running since January 2023 — is the wound. The only cure is delivery before the writ: the $45M hospital build visibly under way, the ER nurses hired, a hard date for 24/7 service. If the ER is open around the clock by summer 2028, her best thirty seconds is gone. If it isn't, no message saves the north end.

Treat this as a governing deliverable with a campaign deadline.

3

Run at her record, not her résumé

Attacking a hometown doctor's credentials fails. What is attackable: the letter she signed on legislature letterhead defending Aaron Gunn's residential-school comments — which even her own colleague Brennan Day publicly disowned — her COVID-measures record, and a party that fired its own leader mid-term. "Good doctor, wrong party" lets her 2020 NDP voters come home without shame.

4

Stop the bleeding in the double-tide villages — with money, not messaging

Sayward +29, Woss +24, Tahsis +24, Gold River +22. Small in votes, huge in narrative — and 639 is smaller. Forestry transition delivery in the Nation-partnership mould, aquaculture transition money with names and dates before the 2029 ban bites Campbell River and Port Hardy. Salmon and paycheques in the same sentence, never climate-first abstractions.

5

Raise the fortress floor

Alert Bay is 58% NDP — it was 77 in 2017. The islands and First Nations communities vote orange on modest turnout, and the federal race proved the mobilizer exists: these same communities went two-thirds federal-NDP against Gunn, whose comments Kindy defended in writing. A dedicated Indigenous-and-islands turnout program is the cheapest 400 votes in the riding.

6

Win Campbell River's advance vote

More of this riding's election-day ballots are cast in Campbell River than everywhere else combined, and the city broke 49.6–43.2 — in a union town with the We Wai Kai and Wei Wai Kum inside city limits and an NDP tradition one election deep in the past. Bank the base early: a hospital-workers, forestry-retirees and First Nations advance-vote drive in Campbell River is where a 639-vote seat is physically won.

7

Name the candidate early — the ceiling depends on it

Babchuk took 44.9% in the worst provincial climate the BC NDP has faced since 2001, and now leads the We Wai Kai Nation's administration — exactly the labour-Indigenous-civic profile this coalition needs. Her or a successor: the candidate must be in the field early enough to out-local a hometown incumbent physician. A late nomination concedes play three.

The rematch arithmetic

639 votes. Two years to close them.

Same coast, same day, a different disease: next door in Courtenay–Comox the Conservatives won with 38.8% on a three-way split — 93 votes. Two seats, 732 votes, one campaign. Read the companion.
